name: Monaco and the Riviera: Nice, Cannes, Menton, Antibes

cities.base: Vieux-Nice, for the old-town restaurants, Castle Hill and the Promenade on foot; every other base is one direct TER train away.
cities.name: Nice

cities.base: Monte-Carlo near the Casino square, or La Condamine for less. Prices jump for the Grand Prix, 3 to 6 June 2027 (to be confirmed), and the Masters, 3 to 11 April 2027.
cities.name: Monaco

cities.base: Le Suquet for the old town and Forville market, or La Croisette for the seafront; both walk to the Vieux Port boats for Sainte-Marguerite.
cities.name: Cannes

cities.base: The old town by the Halles, a walk from the Cocteau Bastion and the basilica steps; the next stop east of Monaco on the same line.
cities.name: Menton

cities.base: Inside the walled old town, next to the Marche Provencal and the Picasso museum; Juan-les-Pins and the Cap are a bus or a long walk.
cities.name: Antibes

places.name: Bar des Oiseaux
places.note: Bistro with house-made pasta: order the calamari ravioli or the bourride. The 20 euro lunch menu is the deal, mains 18 to 24 euros; lunch 12:00 to 13:30, dinner from 19:00, book ahead and ask to avoid the noisy back room.

places.name: Olive & Artichaut
places.note: Bib Gourmand farm-to-table Nicois cooking; the 39 euro Petit menu d'olive is the order, mains 22 to 26 euros. Lunch 12:00 to 13:30, dinner 19:00 to 21:30, Tuesday to Saturday; reserve directly.

places.name: Fine Gueule
places.note: Old-town bistro with a 22 euro lunch menu and a 39 euro dinner menu, mains 22 to 28 euros. Kitchen shuts 14:00 to 19:00, and it is closed Sunday and Monday.
places.neighborhood: Vieux-Nice, rue de l'Hotel de Ville

places.name: Keisuke Matsushima
places.note: French-Japanese tasting-style cooking; the 48 euro seasonal menu is the sensible way in, the 160 euro Menu Patrimoine the splurge. Lunch to 14:00, dinner from 19:00, Tuesday to Saturday.

places.name: Comptoir du Marche
places.note: Market-led bistro: monkfish at 23 euros or the Angus rib steak at 28, about 50 to 60 euros a head. Sources disagree on whether it serves through the afternoon, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Chez Acchiardo
places.note: Family Nicoise kitchen since 1927; order the stuffed vegetables, the daube or the gnocchi, plat du jour 15 to 18 euros. Lunch 12:00 to 14:00, dinner 19:00 to 22:00, closed Saturday and Sunday.

places.name: La Merenda
places.note: Tiny Nicoise classic with dishes at 18 to 22 euros, cash only, and no phone or web booking found, so turn up at opening. Lunch 12:00 to 14:00, dinner 19:00 to 21:30, closed weekends.

places.name: Chez Palmyre
places.note: One 22 euro menu of home cooking: daube or grilled fish. One source says lunch and dinner, closed Wednesday and weekends, another says lunch Monday to Saturday, so hours vary, check before you go.

places.name: Type 55
places.note: Mediterranean cooking and pizza with a 37 euro set menu, and a 22 euro three-course lunch Tuesday to Saturday. Kitchen breaks 14:00 to 19:00; closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Le Bistro Gourmand
places.note: Open every day, which matters in Vieux-Nice on a Sunday or Monday: 42 euro Menu Gourmand at dinner, a 27 euro three-course lunch on weekdays. Lunch to 14:00, dinner from 19:00.

places.name: Le Bistrot de Jan
places.note: Port-side bistro with a 27 euro two-course and 32 euro three-course lunch. Closed Monday per one guide; hours vary, check.

places.name: Chez Pipo
places.note: The socca counter: order a portion of socca, 3 to 6 euros, and a glass of rose. Open Wednesday to Sunday 11:30 to 14:30 and 17:30 to 22:00, closed Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Colline du Chateau (Castle Hill)
places.note: Hill of the old citadel, free, with a waterfall and the full sweep of the Baie des Anges. Give it 90 minutes and go early; 20:00 is the summer closing, winter may be earlier, check.

places.name: Musee Matisse
places.note: Matisse's own museum in Cimiez, next to the Roman ruins: 10 euros (one source says 12), 10:00 to 17:00 from 1 Nov, 18:00 in summer. Closed Tuesday; the 15 euro 4-day pass covers it. One listing shows it temporarily closed, check.

places.name: Musee national Marc Chagall
places.note: Built for Chagall's Biblical Message series; 10 euros, 12 during exhibitions, not in the city pass. Nov to Apr 10:00 to 17:00 with a 13:00 to 14:30 break; closed Tuesday.

places.name: Musee d'Archeologie de Nice-Cimiez
places.note: The Roman town of Cemenelum: baths and an amphitheatre beside the Matisse museum, so do both in one Cimiez half-day. 5 euros or in the 15 euro pass; closed Tuesday, winter hours vary, check.

places.name: Musee du Palais Lascaris
places.note: 17th-century Baroque palace of the Lascaris-Ventimiglia family in the old town. Sources disagree on the ticket, so check the price, or use the 15 euro municipal pass; closed Tuesday.

places.name: Cathedrale Sainte-Reparate
places.note: Baroque cathedral on Place Rossetti, free. Tuesday to Saturday it shuts 12:00 to 14:00, Sunday it runs straight through, Monday closed.

places.name: Cathedrale orthodoxe russe Saint-Nicolas
places.note: The Russian Orthodox cathedral west of the station, about 40 minutes inside. Listed as free, though an entry fee is common, so check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Promenade des Anglais
places.note: The 7 km seafront boulevard along the Baie des Anges, free. Walk it early in the morning, before the runners give way to the crowds.

places.name: Caffe Milano
places.note: Mediterranean on the harbour; the lunch formula of main, glass of wine and coffee runs 22 to 26 euros, a la carte 20 to 40. A starter adds 22 euros or more.

places.name: Quai des Artistes
places.note: Belle Epoque brasserie on the port since 1999; the 32 euro menu du jour is a weekday lunch deal, not on public holidays. Opens 08:00 on weekdays, 10:00 at weekends.

places.name: La Saliere
places.note: Italian on the Fontvieille quay: pasta, risotto, pizza and fish. Three lunch menus at 23, 25 and 27 euros each include coffee and house wine.

places.name: La Note Bleue
places.note: Chef Laurent Paya's beach restaurant on Larvotto since 2002, with a 25 euro lunch tasting menu. Listed daily 09:00 to 22:00, but a winter closure is not ruled out, check.

places.name: MayaBay
places.note: Thai and Japanese: the 29 euro lunch of starter, main, dessert, water and coffee, 35 with wine, is the way to eat here. Dinner is the expensive end of Monaco.

places.name: Les Perles de Monte-Carlo
places.note: Oyster bar on the quay: a dozen No.3 oysters with a glass of organic white for 36 euros. Lunch 12:00 to 14:30, dinner Tuesday to Friday too; closed Sunday.

places.name: La Table d'Elise
places.note: French cooking with a 32 euro lunch set menu and a 52 euro market menu. Monday to Saturday, closed Sunday.

places.name: Oceanographic Museum
places.note: Aquarium and museum in Monaco-Ville; 20.50 euros, give it 2.5 hours, last entry 30 minutes before close. Open daily except 25 Dec and the Grand Prix weekend (3 to 6 June 2027, to be confirmed).

places.name: Jardin Exotique de Monaco
places.note: Cactus garden on the cliff: 12 euros garden only, 15 with the cave or the botanical centre, 18 for all. Nov to Jan 09:00 to 17:00, Feb to Apr and Oct to 18:00.

places.name: Cathedrale de Monaco (Notre-Dame-Immaculee)
places.note: The cathedral on the Rock, free, 09:00 to 18:00. Thirty minutes, best paired with the Palace square and the Oceanographic Museum on the same morning.

places.name: Musee d'Anthropologie prehistorique
places.note: Small prehistory museum beside the Jardin Exotique, so do the two together. Listed at 5 euros, though some visitors report about 1 euro, check the price.

places.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco, State Apartments
places.note: Seasonal: the State Apartments run roughly 30 Mar to 15 Oct (about 17 dollars), so expect them closed in winter. The square and the changing of the guard outside are free all year.

places.name: Eglise de Sainte-Devote
places.note: The patron saint's chapel at the foot of the Sainte-Devote corner of the Grand Prix circuit (race 3 to 6 June 2027, to be confirmed). No entry price listed, check the price; 20 minutes.

places.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo
places.note: The gaming rooms open to visitors after 14:00; a bookable entry is about 22 dollars including 10 euros of credit. Dress code and ID rules not checked, and hours vary, check.

places.name: La Cave
places.note: Traditional cooking with an 18 euro lunch formule and 23 euro lunch menu. Lunch and dinner Tuesday to Friday, dinner on Monday and Saturday, closed Sunday.

places.name: Le Bistrot Gourmand
places.note: French bistro below Le Suquet: 29 euro lunch formula, 35 euro lunch menu, 47 euro seasonal menu. Sunday is lunch to 14:00, Monday closed; not the Nice place of the same name.

places.name: Cote Jardin by Steve Moracchini
places.note: Modern Mediterranean with a 27 euro lunch formula and a 35 euro lunch menu. Tuesday to Saturday, lunch to 14:00 and dinner 19:00 to 21:30.

places.name: Aux Bons Enfants
places.note: Traditional cooking at the foot of Le Suquet; a 41 euro set menu, or a la carte at about 11 for a starter, 21 for a main and 9 for dessert. Closed Sunday.
places.neighborhood: Rue Meynadier, foot of Le Suquet

places.name: L'Eponyme
places.note: French-Mediterranean with a 28 euro lunch special and 34 euro lunch menu. Tuesday to Saturday lunch and dinner, Monday dinner, closed Sunday.

places.name: Le Grain de Sel
places.note: A lunch place, 12:00 to 14:00 Monday to Saturday, with a 19 euro formule midi. Closed Sunday; the cheapest sit-down lunch on this list.

places.name: Le Suquet
places.note: The old hill quarter above the Vieux Port, free and open at all hours. Climb it late afternoon to Notre-Dame d'Esperance and the Castre for the view over the bay.
places.neighborhood: Old hill above the Vieux Port

places.name: Fort Royal and Musee du Masque de Fer
places.note: State prison from 1685 that held the Man in the Iron Mask, given its final shape by Vauban. Shuttle boats leave the Vieux Port daily; check the price of ticket and boat. Oct to Mar 10:30 to 13:15 and 14:15 to 16:45, closed Monday.

places.name: Notre-Dame d'Esperance
places.note: The church at the top of Le Suquet beside the Castre, with a view over the bay. No entry price listed, check the price; 30 minutes, 09:00 to 17:00.

places.name: Musee des Explorations du Monde (Castre)
places.note: In the Chateau de la Castre, a fortified monastery begun by the Lerins monks in the 11th century; 6.50 euros, free first Sunday Nov to Mar. Oct to Mar 10:00 to 17:00 with a 13:00 break, closed Monday. One source says temporarily closed, check.
places.neighborhood: Le Suquet, rue de la Castre

places.name: Palais des Festivals et des Congres
places.note: The current Palais opened in Dec 1982 on the old municipal casino site; the first (1949) hosted the Film Festival. Steps and outside are free; the interior opens for events only.

places.name: Chemin des Etoiles
places.note: Film stars' handprints set in the forecourt beside the Palais des Festivals, free and open at all hours. Fifteen minutes on the way along the Croisette.

places.name: La Croisette
places.note: The seafront boulevard, listed in France's general inventory of cultural heritage. Free; walk it from the Palais east at the end of the day.

places.name: Marche Forville
places.note: Henri Bret's 1930s market hall, opened 1932 and carrying the 20th-century heritage label. Weekdays to 12:30, weekends to 13:30; renovation work may close part of it, check.

places.name: Le Bistrot des Jardins
places.note: Mediterranean cooking with a 47 euro menu. Tuesday to Saturday lunch and dinner, Sunday lunch, closed Monday.

places.name: JR Bistronomie
places.note: Dinner-only bistronomy in the old town, Monday to Saturday; starters 15, mains 28 and desserts 9 euros. Some review sites mix it up with a ceramics studio, so confirm before you book.

places.name: Le Righi
places.note: Traditional cooking up in Sainte-Agnes, about 4 km from Menton, mains 16 to 22 euros, 20 to 25 a head. You need the bus or a car; closed Wednesday.

places.name: Le Beausejour
places.note: Lunch in the hill village of Gorbio, 31 euro set menu, 12:00 to 14:00. Closed Wednesday; you need the bus or a car up from Menton.

places.name: Musee Jean Cocteau, Le Bastion
places.note: A 17th-century seafront fort turned Cocteau museum, about 6 dollars. 10:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesday and public holidays; winter hours vary, check.

places.name: Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange
places.note: Baroque basilica founded in 1653, on the old town parvis. Interior listed 15:00 to 17:00 Monday to Friday plus Saturday morning, which looks partial, so check; no price listed, check the price.

places.name: Jardin botanique Val Rahmeh
places.note: Botanical garden in Garavan, about 9 dollars, an hour. 10:00 to 18:00 are summer hours and winter is not shown, check; closed Tuesday.

places.name: Salle des Mariages Jean Cocteau
places.note: The town hall wedding room Cocteau painted, 2 euros, 20 minutes. Weekdays 08:30 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 16:30; a wedding can close it.
places.neighborhood: Town hall, rue de la Republique

places.name: Marche des Halles de Menton
places.note: The covered market on the quay, mornings 08:00 to 13:00, closed Monday. Go early for picnic food before the old town climb.

places.name: Cimetiere du Vieux Chateau
places.note: Hilltop cemetery above the old town, with views over the bay; free, no gate fee reported. Open 07:00 to 19:00, 45 minutes.

places.name: Jardin d'agrumes du Palais Carnoles
places.note: Citrus garden of the former Grimaldi palace, free per visitors, with a 10 euro guided tour. Open 09:00 to 18:00, Thursday to 17:00; the palace museum hours were not found.

places.name: Musee de Prehistoire Regionale
places.note: Opened 1909: regional prehistoric collections and Mediterranean shipwreck finds. Free under 18 and on the first Sunday, otherwise check the price; 10:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesday.

places.name: La Taille de Guepe
places.note: Traditional Mediterranean in the old town: 21 euro lunch formule, 42 euro menu. Tuesday to Saturday, lunch to 14:00 and dinner from 19:00.

places.name: Nacional
places.note: Italian on Place Nationale with a 38 euro menu. Lunch and dinner most days, but Thursday is dinner and Sunday lunch; closed Monday.

places.name: Le Vauban
places.note: Old-town restaurant with a 29 euro lunch formule and a 49 euro menu. Wednesday to Sunday lunch and dinner, closed Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: La Cafetiere Felee
places.note: Signature cooking at about 36 euros for the formule. Wednesday to Saturday lunch and dinner, Tuesday dinner, closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Musee Picasso, Chateau Grimaldi
places.note: Picasso's work in the Chateau Grimaldi: 12 euros, or 15 for the combined municipal pass. Mid-Sep to mid-Jun 10:00 to 13:00 and 14:00 to 18:00; closed Monday and 1 Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov, 25 Dec.

places.name: Fort Carre
places.note: Star fort north of Port Vauban, an hour. Single ticket is quoted at 3 to 5 euros, so check the price, or use the 15 euro combined museum ticket; closed Monday, and the access road may be diverted for path works.

places.name: Marche Provencal
places.note: The covered market on Cours Massena, 07:00 to 13:00 Tuesday to Sunday, closed Monday. Go before 10:00 and do the Picasso museum next door after.

places.name: Cathedrale d'Antibes
places.note: The old-town cathedral beside the Picasso museum, free. It shuts 12:00 to 15:00, so look in before noon or after 15:00.

places.name: Musee Peynet et du dessin humoristique
places.note: Cartoon and drawing museum on Place Nationale, 5 euros or in the 15 euro combined ticket. 10:00 to 12:50 and 14:00 to 18:00, closed Monday and 1 Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov, 25 Dec.

places.name: Sentier du Littoral, Cap d'Antibes
places.note: The coastal path round Cap d'Antibes, free and open at all hours, about 4 km from the old town. Allow two hours and go in the morning light.

places.name: Juan-les-Pins
places.note: The resort quarter named in 1882, a railway station a year later and Frank Jay Gould's Hotel Provencal finished in 1927. Free; walk the village and the beach.

places.name: Port Vauban
places.note: The superyacht marina under the ramparts on the Fort Carre side, free and open at all hours. Walk it at dusk on the way to dinner in the old town.

places.name: Phare de la Garoupe
places.note: The lighthouse on Cap d'Antibes, rated for its view. No price stated and the interior is not confirmed open, so check the price; hours vary, check.

destination.name: Monaco and the Riviera: Nice, Cannes, Menton, Antibes
destination.pitch: A week on one train line: four nights in Vieux-Nice for socca, Matisse and Chagall, then a night or two each in Monaco, Menton, Antibes and Cannes, none more than 35 minutes from Nice.
destination.caveat: Museums close on set days (Nice Tuesday, Menton Tuesday, Antibes Monday), many old-town kitchens shut Sunday and Monday, the Palace State Apartments close mid-October to spring, and Monaco hotels jump in Grand Prix and Masters weeks. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Nice has a real old town with markets and late dinners, and Monaco puts the Casino, the Palace and the Oceanographic Museum a short walk apart.
because.food: Nicoise cooking at Chez Acchiardo and La Merenda, socca at Chez Pipo, Bib Gourmand Olive & Artichaut, oysters at Les Perles in Monaco, and 20 to 30 euro lunch menus in every town.
because.culture: Matisse and Chagall in Cimiez, Roman Cemenelum, Picasso in the Grimaldi castle at Antibes, Cocteau in Menton, and the Man in the Iron Mask's cell on Sainte-Marguerite.
because.relaxation: Short train hops, long lunches, the Cap d'Antibes coastal path and gardens in Menton and Monaco; nobody needs a car.
because.exploration: Hill villages above Menton for lunch, the Lerins islands by boat from Cannes, and five towns each with their own old quarter.
